purpose: Prior-art seed for the next longevity mission rerun. This record is a source pointer and claim map, not a validated ORACLE finding.
novelty_policy: The 8-mRPG signature and its association with transcriptomic aging are published prior art. ORACLE must not claim this signature itself as a novel discovery.

sources.title: Preserved mitochondrial ribosomal protein gene expression marks a youthful transcriptional state in Chinese nonagenarians and centenarians
claims: The abstract reports 1,751 analyzed individuals (811 LLIs and 940 younger controls); the Methods section reports 1,752 recruited individuals (811 LLIs and 941 younger controls), with one previously published sample excluded for missing age.
Eight mitochondrial ribosomal protein genes showed upward deviation from the typical age-related decline trajectory in long-lived individuals.
The 8-mRPG expression score was associated with lower transcriptomic aging and senescence-related scores.
The authors report replication of the signature pattern in additional longevity cohorts, including the Leiden Longevity Study.
limitations: The study is observational and cross-sectional; it does not establish that mRPG expression causes longevity.
The upstream regulatory processes maintaining mRPG expression remain unknown.
The authors call for functional experiments and note residual confounding may remain.

The counts reconcile arithmetically: 1,752 recruited (811 LLI + 941 YC); 442 previously published (171 CRA000515 + 271 HRA000656); one missing-age sample excluded, leaving 441 prior samples; plus 1,310 new samples = 1,751 analyzed (811 LLI + 940 YC). The identity/accession of the excluded sample remains unknown.

data_accessions.note: Count reconciliation: 171 CRA000515 + 271 HRA000656 = 442 previously published; one previously published sample with missing age was excluded, leaving 441 analyzed prior samples. Adding 1,310 newly generated samples gives 1,751 analyzed participants. The excluded sample's accession/alias remains unidentified.

next_checks: Obtain sample-level metadata and mapping for CRA000515 aliases.
Verify the integrated expression matrix sample annotations and cohort overlap before treating datasets as independent.
Reproduce the 8-mRPG signature with the published code and exact cohort splits.
Test robustness to leukocyte composition, sex, region, sequencing batch, and age.
Generate and experimentally test upstream-regulator hypotheses; do not infer causality from expression associations.

sources.title: Mitonuclear protein imbalance as a conserved longevity mechanism
claims: MRPS5 and other mitochondrial ribosomal proteins were implicated in lifespan regulation using mouse genetics and C. elegans RNAi.
MRP knockdown induced mitonuclear protein imbalance, reduced mitochondrial respiration, activated UPRmt, and extended C. elegans lifespan.
limitations: Functional evidence is mainly from model organisms and cells; it does not establish human longevity causality.
Intervention direction differs from the higher-than-age-expected expression of selected mRPGs in long-lived humans; dose, tissue and timing may matter.

sources.title: Ribosome profiling analysis of human skeletal muscle identifies reduced translation of mitochondrial proteins with age
claims: Human skeletal-muscle ribosome profiling found lower ribosome occupancy for several mitochondrial-genome-encoded oxidative-phosphorylation transcripts with older age.
limitations: This does not measure the nuclear-encoded 8-mRPG signature or exceptional longevity; mitochondrial-genome-encoded OXPHOS translation is a distinct readout.

sources.title: Mendelian randomization analyses implicate biogenesis of translation machinery in human aging
claims: Mendelian-randomization analyses reported associations between genetically proxied expression of Pol I/III and ribosomal-protein machinery and human longevity.
Reduced expression of translation machinery in several tissues was reported as longevity-associated.
limitations: This is not specific to mitochondrial ribosomal proteins; causal interpretation depends on instrument validity and does not validate the 8-mRPG signature.

sources.title: ETS1 acts as a regulator of human healthy aging via decreasing ribosomal activity
claims: Transcriptomes from 185 long-lived individuals and 86 offspring spouses in two Chinese cohorts showed downregulation of the cytosolic ribosome pathway.
ETS1 was lower in long-lived individuals; ETS1 knockdown reduced cytosolic ribosomal-protein expression and cellular senescence in fibroblast models.
limitations: The reported pathway is cytosolic ribosome biogenesis, not the mitochondrial 8-mRPG signature; fibroblast assays do not establish organismal lifespan causality.

sources.title: Transcriptome evidence reveals enhanced autophagy-lysosomal function in centenarians
claims: The study analyzed peripheral-white-blood-cell transcriptomes from 76 centenarians, 54 centenarian offspring and 41 offspring spouses from Hainan.
Autophagy-lysosomal pathway expression was increased in centenarians; CTSB, ATP6V0C, ATG4D and WIPI1 overexpression promoted autophagy and delayed senescence in IMR-90 cells.
Overexpression of the Drosophila WIPI1 homolog Atg18a extended fly lifespan.
limitations: The human evidence is observational and cross-sectional; cell and fly perturbations do not establish human longevity causality.
The cohort was female-heavy among centenarians and the authors noted this limits generalization.
This 171-person cohort is the same Hainan cohort represented by the 171 CRA000515 records; it is not an independent cohort replication.

data_accessions.cra: CRA000515 (171 records cross-referenced; individual age/group labels remain unavailable)

sources.title: Gene expression profiles in the Leiden Longevity Study
limitations: The 2026 paper already cites GSE16717 as a validation cohort; ORACLE reanalysis is a reproducibility check, not a new independent cohort.
The GEO record reports 50 samples per group; individual age/sex metadata coverage must be checked before covariate-adjusted claims.
Normalized microarray expression is not directly comparable to RNA-seq counts.

sources.title: A comprehensive single-cell atlas of three centenarian cohorts unveils unique natural killer cell signatures and enhanced mutual interactions among peripheral immune cells
claims: The study integrated PBMC single-cell RNA-seq from three reported centenarian cohorts: Lingao (17 CEN, 9 offspring, 14 controls), Rugao (7 CEN, 6 offspring, 9 controls) and Japan (7 CEN, 2 offspring, 3 controls); the paper reports a combined 31/17/26 cohort count.

Across cohorts, the authors reported fewer B cells and CD4 T cells and more NK cells in centenarians than controls; NK cells showed relatively young subset/receptor signatures and increased RUNX3/KLF4 activity.
In the new Lingao cohort, CyTOF and flow cytometry provided orthogonal validation of selected immune-cell composition and RUNX3 findings.
limitations: This is evidence for immune-cell remodeling, not direct replication of the 8-mRPG or autophagy-lysosome gene signatures.

The 2025 atlas reuses the Rugao cohort HRA002867 from the 2022 Rugao study and a Japanese cohort from RIKEN SC2018; do not count these as new independent cohorts a second time. The Lingao cohort is the additional cohort.

The new Lingao raw data are deposited as HRA011570 and are controlled-access; HRA002867 is also controlled-access. Sample-level reanalysis requires authorized GSA-Human access and a source-authenticated manifest.
Bulk-blood expression differences may reflect immune-cell proportions or cell states; mRPG expression should be tested within cell types before inferring a cell-intrinsic mitochondrial mechanism.

independent_evidence.design: mouse genetics plus C. elegans RNAi and mammalian-cell experiments
independent_evidence.finding: MRPS5 and other mitochondrial ribosomal protein perturbations induced mitonuclear protein imbalance and UPRmt; MRPS5 knockdown extended C. elegans lifespan.
independent_evidence.relevance: Functional model-organism evidence that mitochondrial translation perturbation can influence lifespan.
independent_evidence.limitation: Direction differs from the higher-than-age-expected expression of selected mRPGs reported in long-lived humans; model-organism intervention is not proof of human causality.

independent_evidence.design: human skeletal-muscle ribosome profiling across middle-aged and older adults
independent_evidence.finding: Older age was associated with lower ribosome occupancy for multiple mitochondrial-genome-encoded oxidative-phosphorylation transcripts.
independent_evidence.relevance: Independent human tissue evidence that mitochondrial translation is age-sensitive.
independent_evidence.limitation: Does not measure the 8-mRPG signature or exceptional longevity; mitochondrial-genome-encoded OXPHOS translation is distinct from nuclear-encoded mitochondrial ribosomal-protein transcript abundance.

independent_evidence.design: human Mendelian-randomization analysis of translation-machinery expression
independent_evidence.finding: Genetically proxied expression of Pol I/III machinery and ribosomal-protein genes was associated with human longevity; reduced expression in several tissues was reported as longevity-associated.
independent_evidence.relevance: Supports a possible global/cytosolic translation-reduction arm of healthy aging.
independent_evidence.limitation: Not specific to mitochondrial ribosomal proteins; MR depends on instrument validity and does not validate the 8-mRPG mechanism.

independent_evidence.design: two Chinese longevity cohorts plus cell perturbation assays
independent_evidence.finding: 185 long-lived individuals and 86 offspring spouses showed downregulated cytosolic ribosome pathway; ETS1 was lower in long-lived individuals and ETS1 knockdown reduced cytosolic ribosomal-protein gene expression and cellular senescence in fibroblast models.
independent_evidence.relevance: Provides a plausible contrast between reduced cytosolic ribosome biogenesis and preserved selected mitochondrial ribosomal transcripts.
independent_evidence.limitation: Cytosolic ribosomal genes are not mitochondrial ribosomal genes; cell assays do not establish a whole-organism longevity mechanism.

independent_evidence.design: 171-person Hainan cohort transcriptomics plus IMR-90 cell and Drosophila perturbation experiments
independent_evidence.finding: Autophagy-lysosomal pathway expression was upregulated in centenarians; selected genes promoted autophagy and delayed cell senescence, while Drosophila Atg18a overexpression extended lifespan.
independent_evidence.relevance: Published human longevity-associated pathway with functional support in cell and fly models.
independent_evidence.limitation: No causal human intervention; the 171-person cohort overlaps the CRA000515 cohort and cannot be counted as an independent replication.

independent_evidence.design: CodeLink GPL2895 peripheral-blood microarray; 50 long-lived siblings, 50 offspring and 50 controls/offspring partners
independent_evidence.finding: Public expression profiles permit testing the published mRPG-8 and cRPG-7 panels in the Leiden cohort.
independent_evidence.relevance: Reproducibility check of the 2026 paper's published validation cohort.
independent_evidence.limitation: Not independent of the validation reported in the 2026 paper; microarray platform and possible age/sex covariate limitations.

independent_evidence.design: three-cohort PBMC single-cell atlas with mass cytometry and flow validation in Lingao
independent_evidence.finding: Across Lingao, Rugao and Japan cohorts, centenarians showed higher NK-cell proportions and lower B/CD4 T-cell proportions; NK cells had relatively young signatures with RUNX3/KLF4 activity and enhanced NK–T signalling.
independent_evidence.relevance: Independent cohort-level evidence that peripheral immune-cell composition and cell state are major features of exceptional longevity; supports testing cell composition as an alternative explanation for bulk mRPG signals.
independent_evidence.limitation: Does not test the 8-mRPG signature directly. Rugao and Japan are reused datasets; only Lingao adds a new cohort in this atlas. Lingao HRA011570 and Rugao HRA002867 are controlled-access.

hypothesis_audit.title: Compartment-specific translation allocation in long-lived humans
hypothesis_audit.statement: Long-lived individuals may preserve a selected mitochondrial ribosomal transcript program above age-expected levels while allowing broader cytosolic ribosome biogenesis to decline; this could help maintain mitochondrial protein synthesis without maintaining globally high translation.
hypothesis_audit.key_alternative: Blood-cell composition, regional/batch effects, or survivor/health selection may explain part of the bulk-expression signature.
falsifiable_tests: Recompute the exact 8-mRPG score from frozen sample-level counts in independent cohorts with matched tissue and verified phenotype.
Test the score within sorted or single-cell-defined leukocyte populations and after cell-composition, sex, age, region and batch adjustment.
Test whether the score predicts mitochondrial translation, mitochondrial-encoded OXPHOS protein abundance, respiratory capacity or ATP production.
Use graded perturbation and rescue of the exact published 8 genes in relevant human cell models; measure mitochondrial translation, respiration, UPRmt and senescence.

hypothesis_audit.title: Dose- and tissue-dependent mitonuclear stress hormesis
hypothesis_audit.statement: Partial or transient mitochondrial translation disruption may activate mitonuclear protein imbalance and UPRmt, whereas preservation of a subset of mitochondrial ribosomal genes may be beneficial in selected human tissues or late-life states; effects may be dose-, tissue- and time-dependent.
falsifiable_tests: Run graded rather than binary perturbations of candidate mRPGs and mitochondrial translation regulators.
Measure time-resolved mitonuclear protein stoichiometry, UPRmt, respiration and cell survival.
Determine whether transient versus chronic perturbation produces opposite effects.

hypothesis_audit.title: Bulk-blood cell-composition or health-status confounding
hypothesis_audit.statement: The 8-mRPG bulk-blood association may partly reflect differences in leukocyte subtype proportions, immune activation, medication, nutritional status or cohort selection rather than a cell-intrinsic longevity mechanism.
falsifiable_tests: Repeat analysis with measured cell counts and cell-type deconvolution in every cohort.
Test within-cell-type expression using sorted cells or single-cell RNA-seq.
Adjust for medication, BMI, diet, chronic disease and sequencing/library protocol where available.

hypothesis_audit.title: Autophagy-lysosome maintenance in long-lived humans
hypothesis_audit.statement: A stronger autophagy-lysosomal maintenance program may contribute to cellular maintenance in some long-lived populations, potentially interacting with mitochondrial quality control and ribosome/translation regulation.
hypothesis_audit.key_alternative: The expression signal may reflect sex composition, blood-cell composition, immune state or survivor selection; the cell/fly perturbations may not translate to human lifespan.
falsifiable_tests: Obtain the source-authenticated 171-sample age/cohort manifest and test the published autophagy gene set within the original Hainan cohort without inferring labels.
Test autophagic flux, lysosomal acidification and cargo clearance in relevant human cell models rather than relying only on transcript abundance.
Perturb CTSB, ATP6V0C, ATG4D and WIPI1 individually and in combination with rescue controls; measure senescence and mitochondrial quality-control phenotypes.
Test whether autophagy scores add predictive information beyond the 8-mRPG signature in independent, non-overlapping cohorts.
qualifying_evidence: Supplemental Table S7 reports no p<0.05 age-expression correlation for the 38 upregulated autophagy-lysosomal genes in the middle-aged F1/F1SP subset; this is not evidence for a monotonic age trend in that subgroup.
hypothesis_audit.sample_level_data_blocker: Supplemental File S1 references samples_information.csv with sample IDs, condition, read_type and library_type; that CSV is absent from the public supplement archive.

gates: The 2026 8-mRPG signature is prior art; ORACLE must not claim it as a new discovery.
The 2013 MRPS5/UPRmt intervention literature and 2026 human expression signature have different directions and biological contexts; reconcile rather than cherry-pick.
The 2021 human muscle translation study concerns mitochondrial-genome-encoded OXPHOS translation, not the same nuclear-encoded mRPG transcript signature.
The 2022 ETS1 and Mendelian-randomization findings concern broad/cytosolic translation machinery, not direct replication of the 8-mRPG signature.
No mechanism passes novelty or causality review until independent sample-level replication and functional perturbation/rescue are complete.
The 2018 autophagy-lysosome result uses the same 171-person Hainan/CRA000515 cohort; do not count it as independent cohort replication.
GSE16717 is already used as a validation cohort by the 2026 paper; an ORACLE reanalysis is a reproducibility check, not a new independent cohort discovery.

The 2025 three-cohort single-cell atlas supports immune-cell composition/state as a live bulk-blood confounder, but it does not directly validate the 8-mRPG signature; Rugao and Japan are reused cohorts, while Lingao is the additional cohort.
